# function: parse_ini

Parses the content of an INI-style file (`key = value` lines below `[section]` headers) the way `sysutils_ini_value` reads it with its default `separator`, and returns a map from section name to a map from key to value.

- Keys before the first section header are in the section `""`, which is only present if it has keys. Every other section is present even if it has no keys.
- A section whose header appears more than once is merged; of a key set more than once, the last value wins.
- Keys and values are split at the first `=` and trimmed. A line without `=` is a key with an empty value, like `skip-name-resolve` in `my.cnf`.
- Values are taken literally: quotes and trailing comments are part of the value, because their meaning differs between INI dialects.
- Lines starting with `#` or `;`, blank lines and malformed section headers are skipped. A UTF-8 byte order mark and `\r\n` line endings are handled.

Provider-defined functions need Terraform 1.8 or later, or OpenTofu 1.7 or later, and a `required_providers` entry for `blechschmidt/sysutils`; call it as `provider::sysutils::parse_ini(...)`. It is pure: it only parses its argument, never reads files or looks at the host, so its result is the same during plan and apply. Use `file()` or the [`sysutils_file`](../data-sources/file.md) data source to read the input.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "sysutils_file" "php_ini" {
  path = "/etc/php/8.2/fpm/php.ini"
}

locals {
  php = provider::sysutils::parse_ini(data.sysutils_file.php_ini.content)
}

# Keys before the first [section] header are in the section "".
output "php_memory_limit" {
  value = lookup(lookup(local.php, "PHP", {}), "memory_limit", null)
}
```

## Signature

<!-- signature generated by tfplugindocs -->
```text
parse_ini(content string) map of map of string
```

## Arguments

<!-- arguments generated by tfplugindocs -->
1. `content` (String) The INI content, for example from `file()` or the `content` of the `sysutils_file` data source.
